sections.title: NRN PLAINS/UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: ZONAL WLY FLOW WILL EXIST ACROSS THE NCNTRL STATES TODAY AS THE EXIT REGION OF A MID-LEVEL JET MOVES INTO THE REGION FROM THE WEST. THIS FEATURE WILL HELP CREATE STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR PROFILES FAVORABLE FOR SEVERE STORMS. AT THE SFC...A LOW IS FORECAST TO DEEPEN ACROSS ECNTRL SD WITH A CORRIDOR OF LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE EXTENDING FROM THE MID-MO VALLEY NWD INTO ERN SD AND SW MN BY LATE AFTERNOON. SFC DEWPOINTS APPEAR LIKELY TO REACH THE MID TO UPPER 60S F WITH MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY IN PLACE BY AFTERNOON ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR. THE MODELS ARE IN GENERALLY GOOD AGREEMENT DEVELOPING THUNDERSTORMS IN ERN SD AND MOVING AN CLUSTER OF STRONG CONVECTION EWD ACROSS SRN MN THIS EVENING. FORECAST SOUNDINGS AT 00Z/MON IN ERN SD SHOW MLCAPE FROM 2500 TO 3000 J/KG WITH AN IMPRESSIVE SHEAR ENVIRONMENT. 0-6 KM SHEAR IS FORECAST TO INCREASE DURING THE DAY REACHING 50 TO 55 KT BY EARLY EVENING. THIS ALONG WITH A STRENGTHENING 40 TO 50 KT LOW-LEVEL JET SHOULD BE FAVORABLE FOR TORNADIC SUPERCELLS. FORECAST SOUNDINGS NEAR AND JUST EAST OF ABERDEEN AT 00Z/MON SHOW 0-3 KM STORM RELATIVE HELICITIES OF 350 TO 400 M2/S2 WITH LCL HEIGHTS AROUND 700 METERS SUGGESTING A THREAT FOR STRONG TORNADOES WILL

sections.title: LOWER GREAT LAKES/UPPER OH VALLEY
sections.text: A SHORTWAVE TROUGH IS FORECAST TO MOVE ACROSS THE GREAT LAKES REGION TODAY. AHEAD OF THE SHORTWAVE TROUGH...AN AXIS OF MODERATE INSTABILITY SHOULD DEVELOP FROM THE OH VALLEY NEWD INTO THE LOWER GREAT LAKES. THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT SHOULD OCCUR ALONG THE INSTABILITY AXIS THIS AFTERNOON AS SFC TEMPS WARM. FORECAST SOUNDINGS NEAR CLEVELAND AND CINCINNATI THIS AFTERNOON SHOW MLCAPE VALUES AROUND 2000 J/KG WITH 20 TO 25 KT OF LOW-LEVEL FLOW. THIS ALONG WITH STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES COULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR MARGINALLY SEVERE WIND GUSTS WITH THE STRONGER CELLS LATE THIS AFTERNOON.

sections.title: SRN PLAINS
sections.text: MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY IS SHOULD BE IN PLACE THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS MUCH OF THE SRN PLAINS WHERE THE MODELS DEVELOP SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS. ALTHOUGH DEEP LAYER SHEAR IS FORECAST TO BE AT OR BELOW 30 KT ACROSS MUCH OF THE WARM SECTOR...STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S F MAY BE ENOUGH FOR A MARGINAL WIND DAMAGE THREAT WITH THE STRONGER UPDRAFTS. HAIL MAY ALSO OCCUR IN AREAS WHERE CONVECTION HAS ACCESS TO MAXIMIZED INSTABILITY. ..BROYLES/GARNER.. 06/17/2012

sections.title: ERN SD/MN AREA LATE THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: SURFACE PRESSURE FALLS/CYCLOGENESIS WILL CONTINUE TODAY ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS IN RESPONSE TO THE APPROACH OF AN UPSTREAM SPEED MAX OVER MT...WHICH WILL DRAW LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE NWD FROM KS/NEB TO THE ERN SD AREA BY MID AFTERNOON. THE 12Z ABR SOUNDING SHOWS A MOIST STABLE LAYER NEAR 500 MB WHICH IS FORECAST TO PERSIST IN ASSOCIATION WITH A BROKEN MID-HIGH CLOUD LAYER NOTED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY THIS MORNING. ADDITIONALLY...MORNING OBSERVATIONS SUGGEST THAT BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE MIGHT BE SLIGHTLY OVER-FORECAST FOR THIS AFTERNOON...WITH MID-UPPER 60S MOST PROBABLE. STILL...STEEPENING LAPSE RATES BELOW 600 MB AND SURFACE HEATING IN CLOUD BREAKS WILL RESULT IN WEAKENING CONVECTIVE INHIBITION BY LATE AFTERNOON...WHEN MLCAPE WILL INCREASE TO 2500-3000 J/KG AND CONVECTIVE INITIATION IS EXPECTED NEAR THE SURFACE LOW/TROUGH IN ERN SD. VEERING WIND PROFILES WITH HEIGHT AND SPEED INCREASES ALOFT WILL RESULT IN EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR IN EXCESS OF 40 KT. THE ORIENTATION OF THE DEEP-LAYER SHEAR VECTORS ACROSS THE SURFACE BOUNDARY WILL FAVOR INITIALLY DISCRETE SUPERCELLS WITH A RISK FOR VERY LARGE HAIL IN THE STEEP LAPSE RATE/LARGE BUOYANCY ENVIRONMENT. TEMPERATURE-DEWPOINT SPREADS WILL BE MARGINALL

sections.title: NRN ND THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: THE PRIMARY MID-UPPER SPEED MAX AND ASSOCIATED SYNOPTIC SURFACE LOW WILL MOVE EWD NEAR THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER LATER THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. THOUGH MOISTURE/INSTABILITY WILL BE WEAKER COMPARED TO AREAS FARTHER S AND E...MLCAPE AOA 500 J/KG AND LONG STRAIGHT HODOGRAPHS COULD SUPPORT A FEW ESEWD-MOVING SUPERCELLS AND/OR SHORT LINE SEGMENTS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING AT LEAST ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: UPPER OH VALLEY TODAY
sections.text: A WEAK MIDLEVEL TROUGH AND AN ASSOCIATED LOW-LEVEL CONFLUENCE BAND WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE SLOWLY EWD FROM LOWER MI/INDIANA INTO OH TODAY. LOW-LEVEL MOISTENING ALONG THE CONFLUENCE BAND AND SURFACE HEATING IN CLOUD BREAKS WILL SUPPORT SURFACE-BASED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT BY EARLY AFTERNOON. MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AND DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE RATHER WEAK IN THE WARM SECTOR...BUT BUOYANCY /MLCAPE OF 1000-1500 J PER KG/ COULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR ISOLATED STRONG/DAMAGING GUSTS WITH DOWNBURSTS THIS AFTERNOON. ..THOMPSON/SMITH.. 06/17/2012

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST
sections.text: A STRONG UPPER TROUGH IS CURRENTLY MOVING ACROSS SASKATCHEWAN AND EASTERN MT. THIS SYSTEM WILL MOVE ACROSS THE NORTHERN PLAINS AND BEGIN AFFECTING PARTS OF EASTERN ND/SD AND MN BY LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. AT THE SURFACE 20-30 KNOT SOUTHERLY LOW LEVEL WINDS ARE HELPING TO TRANSPORT MOISTURE NORTHWARD INTO THE DAKOTAS/MN WITH DEWPOINTS NOW IN THE MID 60S AS FAR NORTH AS SOUTHEAST SD. A WEAK SURFACE LOW IS ORGANIZING OVER CENTRAL SD...WHICH SHOULD MOVE EASTWARD INTO MN LATER TODAY AND PROVIDE THE FOCUS FOR SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT. SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS HAVE DEVELOPED ACROSS SOUTHERN MN THIS MORNING AS WARM ADVECTION AND DESTABILIZATION OCCUR. THESE STORMS MAY POSE A RISK OF MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL...BUT THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT IS EXPECTED LATER THIS AFTERNOON. STORMS SHOULD FORM OVER NORTHEAST SD NEAR SURFACE LOW/WARM FRONT AND TRACK EASTWARD INTO CENTRAL MN. STRENGTHENING VERTICAL SHEAR PROFILES WILL PROMOTE SUPERCELLS WITH VERY LARGE HAIL AND A FEW TORNADOES. LOW LEVEL WINDS WILL CONTINUE TO STRENGTHEN THROUGH THE EVENING AS THE STORMS TRACK ACROSS THE MODERATE RISK AREA...WITH A CONTINUED THREAT OF HAIL/TORNADOES. THE POTENTIAL FOR WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WINDS WILL

sections.title: TX
sections.text: A BAND OF RELATIVELY STRONG NORTH-NORTHWEST FLOW ALOFT HAS DEVELOPED ACROSS WEST-CENTRAL TX TODAY. THIS IS CO-LOCATED WITH MODERATELY STRONG SOUTHERLY LOW LEVEL WINDS AND AMPLE MOISTURE/CAPE. SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM IN THIS AREA LATER TODAY...WITH STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND GREATER CONVECTIVE ORGANIZATION SUGGESTING A RISK OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL.

sections.title: OH VALLEY
sections.text: SCATTERED SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS ARE FORECAST TO DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON ALONG AN AXIS FROM OH/WESTERN PA INTO KY/TN. A MOIST AND MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS IS IN PLACE ACROSS THIS REGION...WITH A FEW INTENSE STORMS POSSIBLE. GUSTY WINDS AND HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE IN THE STRONGEST CORES...ALTHOUGH ORGANIZED SEVERE STORMS ARE NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED. ..HART/MOSIER.. 06/17/2012

sections.title: EASTERN DAKOTAS/UPPER MIDWEST
sections.text: NO CHANGES TO PRIOR FORECAST. SEE MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1198 FOR ADDITIONAL DETAILS.

sections.title: WEST-CENTRAL/NORTHWEST TX
sections.text: PRIOR FORECAST REASONING PERSISTS...ALTHOUGH SOME LIMITED SPATIAL ADJUSTMENTS WERE MADE BASED ON OBSERVATIONAL TRENDS IN ACCORDANCE WITH MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1197.

sections.title: LOWER MO RIVER VALLEY
sections.text: ADJUSTMENTS WERE MADE TO INCLUDE MORE OF THE REGION IN LOW SEVERE WIND/HAIL PROBABILITIES. WHILE CONVERGENCE/FORCING FOR ASCENT SHOULD REMAIN MODEST...ASSORTMENT OF NUMERICAL GUIDANCE INDICATE THE POTENTIAL FOR TSTM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING IN VICINITY OF WARM FRONT/INSTABILITY GRADIENT ACROSS THE REGION. SHOULD THIS OCCUR...AT LEAST SOME SEVERE THREAT WOULD EXIST GIVEN THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY /GENERALLY 2500+ J PER KG MLCAPE/ EVEN WITH WEAK VERTICAL SHEAR.

sections.title: OH VALLEY
sections.text: NO CHANGES...SEE DISCUSSION BELOW. ..GUYER.. 06/17/2012 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1124 AM CDT SUN JUN 17 2012/

sections.title: NRN PLAINS/UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: A CLUSTER OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS IS CURRENTLY ONGOING ACROSS FAR NE SD AND WRN MN LOCATED NEAR AN AXIS OF MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY. THE INSTABILITY AXIS EXTENDS NWD FROM WRN IA INTO WRN MN WHERE MLCAPE VALUES ARE ESTIMATED TO BE FROM 2000 TO 3500 J/KG. RADAR TRENDS SUGGEST THE STORMS ARE CURRENTLY ORGANIZING INTO A BOWING LINE SEGMENT WHICH SHOULD MOVE ESEWD ALONG A WARM FRONT AND INSTABILITY GRADIENT ACROSS SCNTRL MN EARLY THIS EVENING. STORM MOTIONS TO THE EAST SOUTHEAST AT 40 TO 50 KT ALONG WITH STRENGTHENING FLOW AT 850 MB SHOULD HELP INCREASE THE WIND DAMAGE THREAT AS THE MCS CONTINUES TO ORGANIZE. THE CURRENT THINKING IS THAT THE MCS WILL LEAVE A PATH OF WIND DAMAGE EXTENDING FROM WCNTRL MN ESEWD TO JUST SOUTH OF MINNEAPOLIS WHERE A 45 PERCENT WIND DAMAGE PROBABILITY CONTOUR HAS BEEN ADDED. ROTATING STORMS THAT CONTINUE TO EXIST WITHIN THE MCS SHOULD HAVE A LARGE HAIL AND/OR TORNADO THREAT. HOWEVER...THE THREAT FOR TORNADOES AND VERY LARGE HAIL SHOULD BECOME INCREASINGLY ISOLATED AS THE STORMS BECOME PROGRESSIVELY LINEAR. AFTER MIDNIGHT...A WIND DAMAGE THREAT MAY PERSIST AS FAR EAST AS CNTRL WI BUT THE THREAT SHOULD BECOME ISOLATED AS THE MCS ENCOUNTERS A WEAKLY UNSTAB

sections.title: TX HILL COUNTRY
sections.text: A CONVECTIVE CLUSTER IS CURRENTLY ONGOING IN THE TX HILL COUNTRY WHERE MESOANALYSIS SHOWS MODERATE INSTABILITY IN PLACE. MLCAPE VALUES ARE ESTIMATED TO BE AROUND 1500 J/KG WITH 0-3 KM LAPSE RATES OF 8.0 C/KM. THIS SHOULD BE ENOUGH FOR STRONG WIND GUSTS OVER THE NEXT HOUR OR SO. HAIL MAY ALSO OCCUR WITH THE STRONGER UPDRAFTS. HOWEVER...THE THREATS ARE EXPECTED TO DIMINISH QUICKLY THIS EVENING AS INSTABILITY DECREASES ACROSS THE REGION. ..BROYLES.. 06/18/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS HAVE DEVELOPED ACROSS PORTIONS OF W-CNTRL TX AND NW TX. ADDITIONALLY DEVELOPMENT IS POSSIBLE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. HOWEVER...THE PROBABILITY OF SEVERE WEATHER WITH THESE STORMS IS LOW AND A WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A WEAK AXIS OF LOW PRESSURE /WHICH MAYBE A REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM LAST NIGHTS TSTMS/ HAS ACTED AS AN IMPETUS FOR TSTM DEVELOPMENT IN THE UNSTABLE AIR MASS ACROSS W-CNTRL TX AND NW TX. THIS THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY SHOULD PERSIST FOR THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. HOWEVER...WEAK SHEAR /EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR AOB 20 KTS/ SHOULD LIMIT STORM ORGANIZATION BUT GIVEN THE MODERATE INSTABILITY /MLCAPE AROUND 2000 J/KG/ A FEW STRONG UPDRAFTS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING ISOLATED SEVERE HAIL/WIND ARE POSSIBLE. MID-LEVEL WIND FIELDS AND LARGE SCALE LIFT WILL INCREASE LATER THIS EVENING AS A SHORTWAVE TROUGH /CURRENTLY LOCATED ACROSS NE NM AND SE CO/ MOVES INTO THE REGION. THIS MAY HELP TO ORGANIZE ANY ONGOING ACTIVITY AS WELL AS SUPPORT NEW DEVELOPMENT. AS A RESULT...OVERALL SEVERE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN ISOLATED FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS BUT CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FOR INCREASED SIGNS OF STORM ORGANIZATION.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP FROM NERN SD INTO SWRN MN THIS AFTERNOON...MOST LIKELY BETWEEN 20-22Z. SUPERCELLS WITH VERY LARGE HAIL WILL BE THE INITIAL PRIMARY THREAT...ALONG WITH A THREAT FOR ISOLATED TORNADOES. STORMS SHOULD EVENTUALLY GROW UPSCALE INTO LINES AND OR CLUSTERS WITH AN INCREASING THREAT FOR DAMAGING WIND.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THIS AFTERNOON A WARM FRONT STRETCHES FROM WRN IA NWWD TO EXTREME SERN MN...NERN SD TO A SFC LOW IN SCNTRL ND. TROUGH AXIS EXTENDS SWD THROUGH WCNTRL SD. AN E-W CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WAS ALSO INDICATED OVER SWRN MN WWD INTO EXTREME ERN SD JUST NORTH OF SIOUX FALLS. WARM SECTOR HAS BEEN DESTABILIZING WHERE PLUME OF 7.5 C/KM MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES HAVE ADVECTED ABOVE MID 60S DEWPOINTS WITH 2000-2500 J/KG MLCAPE INDICATED OVER ERN SD. THE EWD ADVECTING EML HAS CAPPED THE BOUNDARY LAYER AND INHIBITED SURFACE BASED CONVECTIVE INITIATION SO FAR. HOWEVER...AS THE SFC LAYER CONTINUES TO WARM...STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP MOST LIKELY WITHIN ZONE OF ENHANCED CONVERGENCE WHERE THE LLJ INTERSECTS WRN EXTENSION OF OUTFLOW BOUNDARY OVER SWRN MN AND FAR ERN SD. OTHER STORMS MAY DEVELOP FARTHER NORTH FROM SRN ND INTO NRN SD ALONG AND EAST OF SFC TROUGH/DRYLINE AND WITHIN ZONE OF HEIGHT FALLS ASSOCIATED WITH PROGRESSIVE VORT MAX LOCATED OVER EXTREME SRN ALBERTA. VERTICAL SHEAR OF 40+ KT WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORMS INCLUDING SUPERCELLS. TORNADO THREAT WILL BE GREATEST FROM NERN SD INTO SWRN MN ALONG NOSE OF LLJ AND WHERE SLIGHTLY LOWER LCLS EXIST ALONG MOIST AXIS AND WHERE THE BOUNDARY LAYER IS COOLER. STORMS MAY EVENTUALLY EVOLVE INTO CLUSTERS AND LINES WITH A CONTINUING THREAT OF DAMAGING WIND AND LARGE HAIL INTO THE EARLY EVENING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED SVR STORMS ARE POSSIBLE LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. THREAT IS EXPECTED TO BE LOCALIZED...AND A WW WILL NOT BE NEEDED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 2230Z...VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS ENHANCED CUMULUS GROWTH /WHICH HAS YIELDED AN ISOLATED STORM 25 SSW OF IRK/ OCCURRING FROM ROUGHLY THE STJ/MKC VICINITY EWD ACROSS NRN MO AND THEN SEWD TOWARD STL. THE AGITATED CUMULUS FIELD RESIDES INVOF A NWD RETREATING WARM FROM FRONT...WHERE TEMPERATURES ARE NEAR 90F AND DEWPOINTS ARE CLOSE TO 70F. THE WARM/MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER IS AIDING IN STRONG INSTABILITY...WITH MLCAPE VALUES FROM 1500-3000 J/KG PER OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS GUIDANCE. PRESENCE OF LOW-LEVEL SLYS VEERING TO W-NWLY IN THE MIDLEVELS...COMBINED WITH LARGE CAPE...SUGGESTS ISOLATED SVR STORMS POSING A THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE DURING THE REMAINDER OF THE AFTERNOON INTO EARLY NIGHT. HOWEVER...THREAT IS NOT EXPECTED TO BE WIDESPREAD...THUS A WW WILL NOT BE NEEDED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL SHOULD INCREASE ACROSS NORTHEAST SOUTH DAKOTA INTO WEST CENTRAL MINNESOTA BETWEEN NOW AND 00-02Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: INTENSE CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT IS NOW UNDERWAY EAST OF THE SURFACE LOW CENTER...WITHIN A BROAD WARM FRONTAL ZONE...WHERE THE THERMAL GRADIENT HAS BEEN ENHANCED BY OUTFLOW ASSOCIATED WITH EARLY DAY CONVECTION TO THE EAST...AND STRONG BOUNDARY LAYER HEATING TO NEAR 100F TO THE WEST. STRONG LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC WARM ADVECTION IS EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE TO UPSCALE CONVECTIVE GROWTH INTO AN ORGANIZED MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM BY EARLY EVENING...AS ACTIVITY DEVELOPS EAST SOUTHEASTWARD INTO WEST CENTRAL MINNESOTA ON STRONGLY SHEARED 30-40 KT...AND STRENGTHENING...DEEP LAYER WESTERLY MEAN FLOW. HOWEVER... DISCRETE SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT MAY REMAIN PROMINENT INTO THE 00-02Z TIME FRAME. SOME UNCERTAINTY DOES EXIST CONCERNING THE DEGREE OF SATURATION OF THE LOW-LEVEL ENVIRONMENT...EVEN AS STORMS PROPAGATE EASTWARD TO THE COOL SIDE OF THE GRADIENT ACROSS WEST CENTRAL MINNESOTA...TO THE WEST/SOUTHWEST OF ALEXANDRIA. HOWEVER...WITH THE SOUTHWESTERLY 850 MB JET FORECAST TO STRENGTHEN IN EXCESS OF 40-50 KT...LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS...AT LEAST...APPEAR LIKELY TO BECOME INCREASINGLY SUPPORTIVE OF TORNADIC POTENTIAL. ..KERR.. 06/17/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SVR WEATHER THREAT WILL EXIST ACROSS NRN ND AND NWRN MN INTO PART OF THE NIGHT. CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FOR POSSIBLE WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: EVENING MESOANALYSIS SHOWS AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE SITUATED OVER SERN SK...WITH A COLD FRONT EXTENDING SWD INTO THE NRN HIGH PLAINS. WEDGE OF HIGH THETA-E AIR WAS ALSO OBSERVED ADVANCING NWD ACROSS ERN ND. CLUSTERS OF THUNDERSTORMS HAVE DEVELOPED OVER NWRN/N-CNTRL ND...MOVING EWD AT 30-40 KT...AND APPEAR TO BE TIED TO AN UPPER IMPULSE MOVING ACROSS THE REGION. THIS UPR FEATURE MAY AID IN MAINTAINING STORMS AFTER DARK...WITH AN INCREASE IN COVERAGE AND INTENSITY POSSIBLE IF WARM/MOIST SURFACE AIRMASS OVER ERN ND CAN CONTINUE TO ADVECT NWD. DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL WIND SHEAR IS VERY FAVORABLE FOR BOWING THUNDERSTORMS AND SUPERCELLS...WITH AN ATTENDANT THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. IN ADDITION...LOW-LEVEL E-SELYS QUICKLY VEER TO WLY AT 3 KM AGL...WHICH MAY SUPPORT AN ISOLATED TORNADO AS WELL.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A NEW WW LIKELY WILL BE NEEDED EAST OF WW 404 WITHIN THE NEXT 1 TO 2 HOURS...FOR A CONTINUED RISK OF AT LEAST DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND HAIL INTO LATE EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC WARM ADVECTION CONTINUES TO SUPPORT THE EVOLUTION OF AN ORGANIZED MESOSCALE SCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM IN THE PRESENCE OF MODERATELY LARGE CAPE AND STRENGTHENING DEEP LAYER MEAN FLOW AND SHEAR. AS THE SOUTHWESTERLY 850 MB JET STRENGTHENS TO 50+ KT ACROSS PARTS OF THE MID MISSOURI VALLEY INTO THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY THIS EVENING...AND SURFACE COLD POOLS ASSOCIATED THE CONVECTION CONSOLIDATE AND DEEPEN...FORWARD PROPAGATION MAY ACCELERATE...IN AN EASTERLY OR EAST SOUTHEASTERLY DIRECTION ACROSS CENTRAL MINNESOTA THROUGH 01-03Z. THE 00Z SOUNDING FROM MINNEAPOLIS SUGGESTS SUFFICIENT DESTABILIZATION WILL OCCUR ACROSS THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY TO MAINTAIN A RISK FOR STRONG WIND GUSTS AND HAIL ACROSS AREAS NEAR/WEST THROUGH NORTH OF MINNEAPOLIS-ST. PAUL...INTO PARTS OF NORTHWESTERN WISCONSIN... BEFORE ACTIVITY WEAKENS LATE THIS EVENING. ..KERR.. 06/18/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: DAMAGING WIND POTENTIAL EXPECTED TO CONTINUE AT LEAST ANOTHER 1 TO 2 HOURS SOUTHWEST THROUGH SOUTH OF MINNEAPOLIS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONGEST STORMS HAVE BECOME FOCUSED ON THE SOUTHWESTERN FLANK OF THE EAST SOUTHEASTWARD PROPAGATING MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM. THIS ACTIVITY APPEARS SLIGHTLY ELEVATED...BASED WITHIN STRONG LOW-LEVEL WARM ADVECTION JUST TO THE COOL SIDE OF THE EFFECTIVE SURFACE WARM FRONT...SUPPORTED BY INFLOW EMANATING FROM A NARROW TONGUE OF HIGH BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE CHARACTERIZED BY SURFACE DEW POINTS NEAR 70F. AS THE VIGOROUS CONVECTION CONTINUES TO DEVELOP EAST SOUTHEASTWARD ALONG A REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY SOUTH OF MINNEAPOLIS...INTO AREAS OF WISCONSIN NORTH OF LACROSSE BY 05-07Z...INFLOW MAY BECOME CUT-OFF FROM THE RICHER BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE...WITH SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL GRADUALLY DECREASING. UNTIL THEN THOUGH...ANOTHER STRONG DOWNBURST OR TWO APPEARS POSSIBLE ACROSS SOUTH CENTRAL AND SOUTHEASTERN MINNESOTA. ..KERR.. 06/18/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ONGOING BOW ECHO LOCATED OVER WEST CENTRAL WI INTO SERN MN WILL PERSIST EWD OVERNIGHT THROUGH MUCH OF WI...WITH SOME UNCERTAINTY IN THE DEGREE OF SEVERITY AS THIS CONVECTIVE SYSTEM REMAINS PROGRESSIVE. A NEW WW MAY BE NEEDED ACROSS PARTS OF CENTRAL WI AND SERN MN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 06Z...REGIONAL RADAR IMAGERY INDICATED AN ONGOING BOWING SYSTEM EXTENDING FROM WRN CHIPPEWA COUNTY WI SWWD TO NRN WABASHA COUNTY MN AND THEN WWD TO ERN LE SUEUR COUNTY MN. TRENDS IN THE SPEED OF THIS BOW INDICATED SOME SLOWING OF THE FORWARD MOTION BETWEEN 0530-06Z WITH VALUES OF 30-35 KT. THE WEST CENTRAL WI TO NRN WABASHA/GOODHUE COUNTIES MN PORTION OF THE BOW WAS BEGINNING TO TRACK ON A MORE EWD TRAJECTORY SUGGESTING THIS PART OF THE LINE WAS MOVING FARTHER AWAY FROM FAVORABLE LOW LEVEL INFLOW AND MOVING WITHIN WSWLY MEAN FLOW. MEANWHILE...A 50 KT SWLY LLJ WAS CONTINUING TO PROVIDE AN INFLUX OF MODERATE INSTABILITY INTO THE SWRN FLANK OF THIS CONVECTIVE SYSTEM /JUST S OF THE TWIN CITIES METRO WITH A 0555Z 2 INCH HAIL REPORT IN LE SUEUR COUNTY/. THIS REPORT WAS ATTENDANT TO A STRONG UPDRAFT/STORM TRACKING ESEWD. THE 00Z NSSL 4KM/03Z HRRR EACH SUGGEST THIS BOWING SYSTEM WILL PROGRESS EWD ACROSS WI...WITH THE LATTER INDICATING A MORE SEWD TRACK. GIVEN THE RECENT INCREASE IN TSTM INTENSITY ALONG THE SWRN FLANK AND THE LLJ REMAINING PERSISTENT WITH SOME VEERING TO WSWLY...IT IS LIKELY THAT SOME FORM OF THIS BOW WILL PROGRESS ACROSS WI WITH AT LEAST AN ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT...ESPECIALLY ALONG THE SWRN FLANK. IF THE STRONG STORM THAT MOVED FROM LE SUEUR COUNTY TO RICE COUNTY EVOLVES INTO A SECOND BOWING STRUCTURE...THEN AN INCREASED WIND THREAT COULD BE EXPECTED ACROSS CENTRAL WI. ..PETERS.. 06/18/2012
